key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can replace expensive CPFE simulations to optimize polycrystalline microstructures under competing spall and yield strength requirements.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid, full-field design exploration for microstructure optimization in solid mechanics while retaining the ability to assess dynamic response and failure behavior.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D polycrystalline copper microstructures directly to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Surrogate is paired with stochastic microstructure generation and derivative-free optimization to search the design space.
A distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) based on MMD flags when optimization moves beyond the training distribution.
evidence_signal: Validated optimal designs against CPFE with less than 3% prediction error, while reducing cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude versus direct CPFE-based optimization.
watch_item: Performance depends on the surrogate staying within a reliable distributional region, so out-of-distribution microstructures may require additional training or validation.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
